name: Maritime place that cannot answer
text: I am questioned in vain, for I am a maritime place.

name: Bedded Londoner rather than a vagabond
text: I am a member of the human race, a native of Great Britain, and a resident of London. I am a stratus, or a bedded, not a vagabond, member of society. I am a stratus, because I have a fixed place of abode, and because I am not a member of the great army of vagabratage, which has no domicile. I am a Londoner, because I was born in the capital, and have never lived anywhere else. I am a man, because a structure, which is animated, and which has structure, is a man.

name: Commercial premises in Cheapside
text: I am part of a great commercial establishment in Cheapside, London. The premises in which I am contained comprise an extensive range of warehouses, and a counting-house. The warehouses are well and handsomely fitted up, and the whole presents an appearance of great business and activity. I am situated in the very heart of the commercial portion of the city, and can boast of having had some of the most eminent men in the city for my companions. In days gone by, I formed part of the establishment occupied by the celebrated Whittington, and, subsequently, I was portion of the premises long held by Thomas Gresham. In more modern times, I have been part of the establishment of Messrs. Thomas and William Row, and, at present, I am concerned in the business of Messrs. Thomas and James

name: Myself for only a few minutes
text: I am only myself, and I cannot answer for more than a few minutes at a time.

name: Ghost revealing future and secret things
text: I am a ghost. I appear to certain persons, in order togratify their wishes, and to enable them to discover things future or secret. I can also appear of my own free will, and for purposes of amusement. In the former case, my power extends no further than to gratify the curiosity of the person I love; in the latter, I can assume any shape, and exert any degree of influence. I can render myself visible, or invisible, at pleasure; and I can pass through walls, and enter into closed rooms. By these means I have been enabled to procure great riches, and to gratify ardent affection. I have appeared to many, and never failed to fulfil the expectations of any. I have appeared to all sorts of people, and have advised some to good, and

name: Presence, weight, time and space
text: I am presence, being, or existence, in general; my presence is where my being is, and my being is where I exist. I am weight, and I am measure; I am time, and I am space; I am life, and I am death; I am weight, presence, being, and existence, being merely presence continued, and presence being weight, and weight being measure, and measure being time, and time being space, and space being life, and life being death.

name: Second voice and casting vote
text: I am a second voice, or casting vote, in case of an equality, and no more. I am also a second vote, in case of a casting vote, and no less. I am a second, or casting, vote, when two voices are given, and no more, and I am a second voice, when two votes are given, and no less.

name: Walker named Walklate
text: I am a walker, and my name is Walklate. I live in Walworth, and walk to and from my work every day. I walk to the City at eight in the morning, and walk back again in the evening. I walk to walk, and walk to walk.

name: Thousand-year-old observer of London
text: That I am a citizen of no mean city, is evident from the fact that I was born in London, where I have lived for nearly a thousand years, during which time I have seen many changes, and have improved in proportion to the improvements which have been made in the city. I have seen the Thames, which was once a dirty, shallow, and inconvenient river, become a broad, clear, and convenient thoroughfare, in which ships of the greatest size can easily arrive at, and depart from, the metropolis, in almost any part of the world. I have seen the city itself, which was formerly only a few miles in circumference, extended to a vast extent, and the number of inhabitants increased to nearly a million. I have seen the greatest improvements in the buildings, and in the streets

name: Only what I wish to be thought
text: I am what I wish to be thought, nothing more, and nothing less.

name: A voice
text: I am a voice.

name: United Kingdom made of counties
text: I am a member of the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland. I am composed of England, Wales, and Scotland. England contains the counties of Bedford, Berks, Buckingham, Cambridge, Chester, Cornwall, Derby, Devon, Dorset, Gloucester, Hereford, Hertford, Huntingdon, Kent, Lancaster, Leicester, Lincoln, Middlesex, Monmouth, Norfolk, Northampton, Nottingham, Oxford, and Somerset. Wales contains the counties of Anglesea and Carmarthen. Scotland contains the counties of Aberdeen, Argyll, Banff, Berwick, Bute, Clackmannan, Dumbarton, Fife, Forfar, and Inverness.

name: Ninth edition of Scotland’s first printed book
text: I am the ninth edition of the first book published in Scotland, being the first edition of the Psalms of David in metre, printed at Edinburgh in the year 1560, in the reign of the first king of Scotland of the house of Stuart. I am commonly called the first edition of the first Scottish Psalms, and in the later editions I am styled the first part of the first edition. I was published in the year immediately following the establishment of the Reformation in Scotland, and in the very earliest period of the art of printing in the kingdom. I was published in the time of the first and second editions of the first English book, commonly called Matthew’s Bible, and in the first year of the publication of the first German Protestant edition of the Holy Scriptures. I was printed in the first complete

name: City of London at noon
text: I am the City of London, in the hour of noon.

name: Individual made of an aggregate of years
text: I am an individual, whose aggregate of life amounts in the whole to a certain number of years, and whose life, taken separately, is never enjoyed by any one of me in the long run. I am made up of parts, which are each of them individually incapable of enjoyment, but which, when collectively taken, produce in the gross a pleasure below zero in the long run of life. The pleasures of the year please me in the aggregate, but not at all when summed up for each year separately. The pain of the year pains me in the aggregate, but never comes to anything when added up for each year singly. The pleasures of life are painful in the long run, and the pains pleasant.

name: Subscriber to be mailed
text: I am a subscriber, and will be forwarded to you in a few days.

name: Little rivulet
text: I am a little rivulet,

name: Departed Spirit
text: I am a spirit that has left the body, And hover o'er the earth, Where the scenes of my former life are passed in review.

name: Soft-iron keeper
text: I am an English keeper of soft iron, and a permanent magnet. I keep soft iron from becoming a permanent magnet, but I cannot keep myself from becoming a soft iron keeper of permanent magnets. I keep the soft iron of horseshoes from becoming permanent magnets, but I cannot keep myself from becoming a keeper of the soft iron of horseshoes. I keep the soft iron of keepers from becoming permanent magnets, but I cannot keep myself from becoming a keeper of keepers. I keep keepers from becoming permanent keepers of soft iron, but I cannot keep myself from becoming a keeper of keepers of soft iron. I keep soft iron from becoming permanent soft iron, but I cannot keep myself from becoming soft iron. I am a keeper of soft iron, and a keeper of keepers of soft iron. I am

name: Emetic powder sold in white boxes
text: I am a servant of the public, and my name is Emetic. I produce a feeling of nausea, and I promote the cause of emetics. I am a white powder, which is sold in square white boxes. I am administered to people who are sick, and to people who are not sick, but only think they shall be. I act as an emetic, and I act as a gentle, and bloodless, and safe, emetic. I Ipecacuan, and I Tartarised, and I Ipecacuanised, and I Tartarised, Emetic. I Ipecacuanised, and I Tartarised, Emetic, is a compound of Ipecacuan and Tartar Emetic, and I Ipecacuanised, and I Tartarised, Emetic, is a

name: Nine Muses spread across London
text: We are a family of nine, who live in Lambeth, and call ourselves the Nine Muses. We are a united family, from Cornwall to Cumberland, and from Kent to Yorkshire. The eldest sister lives in the West, the youngest in the East; the fair average lies between the two extremes, in the middle. The family are all at home together, from Highgate and Holloway, in the North, to Peckham, in the South. East and West, they meet in St. Paul's Churchyard; and North and South, in Charing Cross. They have a common friend in every square, from Highgate to Charing Cross; and another in the heart of every circle, from St. Paul's to Charing Cross. They shake hands across the Channel; and under the shadow of St. Paul's.

name: Richard Roe unless under oath
text: I am Richard Roe, if I take an oath, I am Richard Roe, if I take not an oath, I am Martin Marprelate.

name: Irregular part of the verb to be
text: I am an irregular part of an irregular verb, to be.

name: Horse
text: I am a horse, belonging to a circle of friends, who have resolved to bear you on the back, at the rate of eight miles a figure-circle, and to deliver you safely within the limits of any figure, which you may yourself designate, at the rate of fifty miles a circle, at the price of six shillings a figure.

name: Steam furnishing power
text: I am steam. When power is wanted, I can furnish it. I can drive machinery, and I can light houses and buildings with brilliancy. I can transport a great many persons speedily and cheaply, and I can warm houses comfortably. In short, I can furnish power.

name: Miller on a stream, part person and part premises
text: I am a miller, situated on the banks of a pleasant stream, in a romantic part of the country. My dwelling has been erected about a hundred years, and, having been thoroughly repaired and enlarged, is now convenient and comfortable. I have a good dwelling-house, and a garden, in which I grow plenty of excellent roots and salads. I have also a small piece of meadow ground, that supplies me with good paper manufacture. I have two sons and a daughter; the eldest son is a clergyman, and the youngest a surgeon; my daughter has been lately married to a draper, and lives about a mile below me, on the same stream.

name: A connection to air through any person’s lungs
text: I am placed in communication with the outer air, through the lungs of any person, by means of a bronchial tube, which is thus put in communication with the atmosphere.
